question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

We went to the mall; however, us only gone window-shopping.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. we only went.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined part "us only gone" has two errors:

◦ "us" is an objective-case pronoun and cannot work as the subject of a clause; the subject form "we" is required.

◦ "gone" is the past participle (V3) and cannot stand alone as a finite verb; it needs an auxiliary (has/had gone). Since the first clause is in the simple past ("We went to the mall"), the second clause must also be simple past — "went".

• Hence "us only gone" must be replaced by "we only went".

◦ Correct: We went to the mall; however, we only went window-shopping.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because the sentence as printed is ungrammatical on both counts above.

• Option 3 "they only going" changes the doer (the subject is "we", not "they") and uses the bare "-ing" form without an auxiliary.

• Option 4 "we only gone" fixes only the pronoun; "gone" still has no helping verb.

NOTE

• Subject pronouns: I, we, you, he, she, it, they. Object pronouns: me, us, you, him, her, it, them.

• Verb forms of "go": go (V1) – went (V2) – gone (V3). V3 is used only with have/has/had/be: "we have gone", never "we gone".

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

Make sure you known how to swim.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. you known.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Known" is the past participle (V3) of "know" and cannot be used as the finite verb of the clause without an auxiliary. After the subject "you", the simple present form "know" is required.

◦ Correct: Make sure you know how to swim.

• The imperative "Make sure" is followed by a noun clause ("(that) you know how to swim"), whose verb must agree with its own subject "you" — hence "know".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Make sure" (Option 3) is a correct imperative expression meaning "ensure".

• "how to swim." (Option 2) is a correct infinitive after a wh-word structure (how + to + V1).

• Since a clear error exists, Option 1 "No error" cannot be selected.

NOTE

• Verb forms of "know": know (V1) – knew (V2) – known (V3). V3 appears only with have/has/had or be: "I have known him for years", "It is known to all".

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

“May I ______ your coats, Mr. and Mrs. Mason?”
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. take.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Take" here means to receive something from somebody in order to look after it. Offering to "take someone's coat" is the standard polite expression used by a host or attendant when a guest arrives. (लेना / संभालना)

◦ Correct: “May I take your coats, Mr. and Mrs. Mason?”

• "May I ..." is a polite request/offer structure and is always followed by the base form (V1) of the verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "taste" means to sample the flavour of food — it cannot apply to coats.

• Option 3 "trek" means to make a long, difficult journey on foot (an intransitive verb of travel).

• Option 4 "track" means to follow the trail of a person or animal — it does not fit an offer of hospitality.

NOTE

• Common hospitality collocations: "take your coat", "show you in", "offer you a drink", "make yourself at home".

• After modal verbs (may, can, could, shall, will, must) always use the bare infinitive: may take, can go, must see.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

They wanted me to (expound) on this topic because I had some decent ideas on the subject.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. expatiate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Expound" means to explain something in detail; to set out an idea at length. Its closest synonym is "expatiate", which means to speak or write at length/in detail on a subject. (विस्तार से समझाना)

◦ Correct: They wanted me to expatiate on this topic because I had some decent ideas on the subject.

• Both verbs are typically followed by the preposition "on/upon": "expound on a theory", "expatiate upon a theme" — which is exactly the structure of the given sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "paucity" is a noun meaning scarcity or a very small amount (कमी) — it is not even the same part of speech.

• Option 2 "notoriety" is a noun meaning fame for something bad (कुख्याति).

• Option 3 "partisan" is a noun/adjective meaning a strong, biased supporter of a party or cause (पक्षपाती).

NOTE

• Synonyms of expound/expatiate: elaborate, elucidate, explicate, enlarge upon, dwell on.

• Antonyms: abridge, condense, summarise, curtail.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

The front part is used for carving / the lines and the back end / for scratching of whole areas.
option_1: the lines and the back end
option_3: The front part is used for carving
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. for scratching of whole areas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The gerund "scratching" is used here as a verb form taking a direct object, so it must be followed directly by its object — the preposition "of" is superfluous.

◦ Correct: The front part is used for carving the lines and the back end for scratching whole areas.

• Compare the parallel first half of the sentence: "used for carving the lines" — no "of" is used there either. Grammatical parallelism therefore also demands "for scratching whole areas".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "The front part is used for carving" is correct — "be used for + V-ing" is the standard pattern for stating purpose.

• Option 1 "the lines and the back end" is correct; it simply completes the first clause and introduces the second subject.

• Option 2 "No Error" cannot be chosen because a clear redundancy exists in the last segment.

NOTE

• A gerund keeps its verbal force: it takes an object directly (writing letters, scratching areas). Adding "of" turns it into a noun-like structure that then needs an article — "the scratching of whole areas" — which does not fit "used for".

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Break sweat
option_3: To use a lot of energy or effort
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To use a lot of energy or effort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "break (a) sweat" means to exert oneself; to work hard enough to perspire, i.e., to use a lot of energy or effort. (कड़ी मेहनत करना / जोर लगाना)

◦ Example: He finished the whole job without breaking a sweat, so easy was it for him.

• The image behind the idiom is physical: real effort makes a person sweat, so "breaking a sweat" = putting in genuine effort.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To make a futile attempt" matches idioms like "flog a dead horse" or "beat the air".

• Option 2 "To lie" matches "spin a yarn" or "tell a tall tale".

• Option 4 "To be caught stealing" matches "be caught red-handed".

NOTE

• Related idioms of hard work: "burn the midnight oil" (study/work late), "put one's shoulder to the wheel", "sweat blood", "leave no stone unturned".

• The negative form "without breaking a sweat" means "very easily, with no effort at all".

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

There can’t be anything positive about plastics with pathogens floating around.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. depreciative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Positive" here means favourable, approving, expressing support or praise. Its antonym is "depreciative", meaning expressing disapproval or criticism; belittling the value of something. (निंदात्मक / अवमूल्यन करने वाला)

◦ Example: Her positive remarks encouraged him, while his depreciative comments discouraged the team.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "approving" (showing agreement/praise) is a synonym of positive, not an antonym.

• Option 2 "flattering" (praising excessively) is also close in sense to positive.

• Option 4 "fundamental" means basic or essential — it is unrelated to the positive/negative axis.

NOTE

• Synonyms of positive: affirmative, optimistic, favourable, constructive.

• Antonyms of positive: negative, depreciative, disparaging, pessimistic, derogatory.

• Note the related words: depreciate (to fall in value / to belittle) vs appreciate (to rise in value / to value highly).

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Curtailed
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Lengthened.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Curtailed" means cut short, reduced or shortened in extent or duration. Its antonym is "lengthened", meaning made longer or extended. (छोटा करना का विलोम — लंबा करना)

◦ Example: The programme was curtailed because of rain, but next year it was lengthened to two days.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Slashed" (cut drastically, especially prices/budgets) is a synonym of curtailed.

• Option 3 "Pruned" (cut back branches; trimmed down) is also a synonym.

• Option 4 "Trimmed" (cut off small amounts to neaten/reduce) is likewise a synonym.

• Three options mean "to cut/reduce"; only "lengthened" moves in the opposite direction — a useful elimination strategy in antonym questions.

NOTE

• Synonyms of curtail: cut back, abridge, truncate, diminish, restrict.

• Antonyms of curtail: lengthen, extend, prolong, increase, expand, augment.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

This is most unique thing I have ever seen in my life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. This is most unique.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• There are two faults packed into this segment:

◦ "Unique" is an absolute (non-gradable) adjective — something is either unique or it is not. It therefore cannot take "more/most/very".

◦ Even if a superlative were allowed, it would need the definite article "the" before it ("the most ..."), which is missing.

• The natural correction is to drop "most" and use the article "the":

◦ Correct: This is the most unusual/the only unique thing I have ever seen in my life — or simply, This is a unique thing I have ever seen in my life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "thing I have ever" is correct; "ever" is regularly used with the present perfect in such superlative-type structures.

• Option 3 "seen in my life." is correct — "seen" is the proper past participle after "have".

• Option 1 "No error" is ruled out by the faulty use of "most unique".

NOTE

• Other absolute adjectives that take no comparative/superlative: perfect, complete, universal, entire, extreme, supreme, ideal, eternal, chief, final, round, square, empty, full.

• Rule: a superlative in English normally requires "the" — "the tallest boy", "the most beautiful painting".

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

It is not that you seem heartless.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. cruel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Heartless" means completely lacking pity or compassion; unfeeling and hard-hearted. Its closest synonym among the options is "cruel". (निर्दयी / निष्ठुर)

◦ Example: It was heartless/cruel of him to abandon the injured puppy.

• The suffix "-less" means "without": heart + less = "without heart", i.e., without feeling.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "robust" means strong and healthy (हृष्ट-पुष्ट) — unrelated to feeling.

• Option 2 "warm" (affectionate, kind-hearted) is an antonym of heartless.

• Option 3 "mild" (gentle, not severe) is also opposite in tone.

NOTE

• Synonyms of heartless: cruel, callous, merciless, ruthless, pitiless, unfeeling, stony-hearted.

• Antonyms of heartless: kind, compassionate, warm, humane, merciful, tender-hearted.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘no substitution required’.

No, they are normal people, (although they perceive the world different).
option_1: but they perceive the world differently
option_3: from they perceive the world differently
option_4: while they perceive the world different
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. but they perceive the world differently.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two corrections are needed in the bracketed segment:

◦ "different" is an adjective, but the word modifies the verb "perceive", so the adverb "differently" is required.

◦ The sentence contrasts two ideas ("they are normal people" vs "they see things in another way"); the coordinating conjunction "but" joins them naturally and idiomatically here.

◦ Correct: No, they are normal people, but they perceive the world differently.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No substitution required" is wrong because "perceive ... different" is grammatically incorrect.

• Option 3 "from they perceive ..." is meaningless — "from" is a preposition and cannot introduce a clause like this.

• Option 4 "while they perceive the world different" still keeps the wrong adjective "different" instead of "differently".

NOTE

• Adjectives modify nouns/pronouns (a different view); adverbs modify verbs, adjectives and other adverbs (they see it differently).

• Most adverbs of manner are formed by adding "-ly": quick → quickly, different → differently, careful → carefully.

question: Four sentences are given, out of which three have spelling errors. Choose the sentence with all correctly spelt words.
option_1: He made the most delicious pumkin pie.
option_2: The paralel lives of two contemporaries.
option_3: She took a pair of sissors and cut his hair.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. I need a strong adhesive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every word in Option 4 is spelt correctly. "Adhesive" means a substance such as glue used for sticking things together. (चिपकाने वाला पदार्थ)

• Spelling key: AD + HE + SIVE (from the verb "adhere" — to stick to).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "pumkin" is misspelt — the correct spelling is "pumpkin" (with a "p" after "pum").

• Option 2: "paralel" is misspelt — the correct spelling is "parallel" (one "r", double "l" in the middle: PAR + AL + LEL).

• Option 3: "sissors" is misspelt — the correct spelling is "scissors" (silent "c": SC + IS + SORS).

NOTE

• Frequently misspelt SSC words worth memorising: parallel, scissors, pumpkin, occurrence, embarrass, questionnaire, maintenance, privilege, receive, separate, definitely.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

He started a newly jobs on Tuesday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a new job.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined part contains two errors:

◦ "newly" is an adverb; the word qualifies the noun "job(s)", so the adjective "new" is needed.

◦ The article "a" is singular, so the noun must also be singular — "job", not "jobs".

• Hence the correct phrase is "a new job".

◦ Correct: He started a new job on Tuesday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because "a newly jobs" is doubly incorrect.

• Option 3 "a new jobs" keeps the article–noun disagreement (a + plural noun).

• Option 4 "an new job" uses "an" before the consonant sound /n/ — "an" is used only before a vowel sound.

NOTE

• Article rule: "a" before a consonant sound (a job, a university, a one-rupee coin); "an" before a vowel sound (an hour, an MP, an apple).

• Adjective vs adverb: "a new job" (adjective + noun) but "a newly built house" (adverb + participle).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To poke one’s nose into
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To interfere.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to poke one's nose into (something)" means to interfere or meddle in other people's affairs without being asked. (दूसरों के मामलों में दखल देना / टाँग अड़ाना)

◦ Example: Stop poking your nose into my family matters.

• The image is of pushing one's nose where it does not belong — hence unwanted intrusion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To give permission" would be "give the green light" or "give the go-ahead".

• Option 2 "To show disrespect" would be "look down upon" or "turn up one's nose at".

• Option 3 "To bring no sense" does not correspond to any standard idiom.

NOTE

• Related "nose" idioms: "lead someone by the nose" (control completely), "turn up one's nose at" (reject scornfully), "keep one's nose clean" (stay out of trouble), "pay through the nose" (pay far too much).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

I strained ______ to catch his options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. hard.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hard" is used here as an adverb of manner meaning with great effort/intensely, and it modifies the verb "strained".

◦ Correct: I strained hard to catch his options.

• "Hard" is one of those words whose adverb form is identical to the adjective (a hard task / to work hard). No "-ly" is added.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hardly" is a negative adverb meaning "scarcely/almost not". "I strained hardly" would absurdly mean "I hardly strained".

• Option 3 "hardest" is the superlative and would need a comparison group plus usually "the".

• Option 4 "hardness" is a noun and cannot modify a verb.

NOTE

• Adverbs with two forms and different meanings: hard (with effort) / hardly (scarcely); late (not early) / lately (recently); near (close) / nearly (almost); high (at a height) / highly (very much).

• "Hardly, scarcely, barely" are negative in sense, so they are never used with another negative word.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Rohan was now standing on tiptoe to ______ over at the inhabitants of the two beds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. look.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb needed must fit the prepositional pattern "______ over at". The natural, idiomatic combination in English is "look over at (somebody)", meaning to direct one's eyes towards someone a little distance away. (नज़र डालना)

◦ Correct: Rohan was now standing on tiptoe to look over at the inhabitants of the two beds.

• "Standing on tiptoe" signals that he is stretching up merely to see across — exactly the casual sense of "look over at".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "view" is a transitive verb taking a direct object ("view the scene"); "view over at" is not an English collocation.

• Option 3 "stare" means to gaze fixedly and takes "stare at", not "stare over at".

• Option 4 "peep" means to look quickly and secretly, usually "peep through/into" a small opening — it does not take "over at".

NOTE

• Verbs of seeing and their prepositions: look at / look over at / look into, stare at, glance at, peep through, gaze upon, glare at.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A group of people who have no permanent abode but wander from place to place
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Nomad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "nomad" is a member of a community that has no fixed home and moves from place to place, usually in search of pasture, water or food. (घुमंतू / खानाबदोश)

◦ Example: The nomads of Central Asia migrate with their herds every season.

• The adjective form is "nomadic" and the way of life is called "nomadism".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Truant" — a pupil who stays away from school without permission.

• Option 3 "Ponderer" — one who thinks deeply about something.

• Option 4 "Usurer" — one who lends money at an unreasonably high rate of interest (सूदखोर).

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: vagabond/vagrant (a wanderer with no settled home or work), itinerant (travelling from place to place for work), emigrant (one who leaves his own country), immigrant (one who comes into a foreign country to settle).

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Artiset.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Artiset" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "artist", meaning a person who creates art — paintings, sculpture, music or other creative work. (कलाकार)

• Spelling key: ART + IST. The suffix "-ist" denotes a person who practises something: artist, scientist, dentist, novelist, pianist.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Banker" (a person who manages or owns a bank), "Robber" (a person who steals using force or threat) and "Teacher" (a person who teaches) are all correctly spelt.

• Note that these three use the agent suffix "-er", while "artist" uses "-ist" — mixing the two is the trap here.

NOTE

• Distinguish the near-look-alikes: artist (a creator of art), artiste (a professional performer such as a singer or dancer), and artisan (a skilled manual worker/craftsman).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Plastic inhabits the oceans, ______ up in the guts of seagulls and great white sharks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. building.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "build up" means to accumulate/collect gradually in increasing quantity. Plastic waste gradually accumulates inside the digestive tracts of sea creatures, so "building up in the guts of seagulls and great white sharks" is the intended sense. (जमा होना / इकट्ठा होना)

◦ Correct: Plastic inhabits the oceans, building up in the guts of seagulls and great white sharks.

• The participle "building" also correctly forms a participial phrase describing what the plastic does.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "burning up" means to be destroyed by fire or to use up energy — plastic does not burn inside a bird's stomach.

• Option 3 "provoking" means to deliberately annoy or incite; it does not take "up" in this sense.

• Option 4 "sailing" means to travel on water by ship — it cannot describe matter collecting inside a gut.

NOTE

• Useful phrasal verbs with "up": build up (accumulate), bring up (raise/mention), give up (quit), take up (start a hobby), put up with (tolerate), turn up (arrive).

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

That can be carried or moved easily
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Portable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Portable" means able to be easily carried or moved, especially because it is light in weight. (सुवाह्य / आसानी से ले जाने योग्य)

◦ Example: A portable speaker can be carried in a bag.

• It comes from the Latin "portare" = to carry (the same root gives us port, porter, transport, export, import).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Illegible" — writing that cannot be read (अपठनीय).

• Option 2 "Handful" — a small quantity that fills the hand, or a troublesome person.

• Option 4 "Potable" — fit to drink (पीने योग्य). "Potable water" means drinking water. Note the near-identical look of portable and potable — a classic SSC trap.

NOTE

• Adjectives ending in "-able/-ible" as one-word substitutes: audible (that can be heard), edible (fit to eat), legible (that can be read), inevitable (that cannot be avoided), incorrigible (that cannot be corrected).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

A young man walks toward me with a stick slung across his back and a (1)______ of sheep at his feet, which carry him down the path (2)______ a crowd of rowdy children. An older man follows, weatherworn but still (3)______, a rifle over his left shoulder. He clicks his tongue to (4)______ the flock. Behind him are two women on horses; I guess (5)______ are his wife and daughter.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. flock.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct collective noun for sheep is a "flock of sheep". (भेड़ों का झुंड)

◦ Correct: ... a stick slung across his back and a flock of sheep at his feet ...

• The passage itself confirms this later: "He clicks his tongue to ______ the flock" — the same word is used for the same group of animals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "army" is used for soldiers or ants (an army of ants).

• Option 2 "shoal" is used for fish (a shoal of fish).

• Option 3 "horde" suggests a large, disorderly crowd of people, not domestic animals.

NOTE

• Common collective nouns: a flock of sheep/birds, a herd of cattle/elephants, a pack of wolves, a swarm of bees, a pride of lions, a school/shoal of fish, a litter of puppies, a gaggle of geese.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

A young man walks toward me with a stick slung across his back and a (1)______ of sheep at his feet, which carry him down the path (2)______ a crowd of rowdy children. An older man follows, weatherworn but still (3)______, a rifle over his left shoulder. He clicks his tongue to (4)______ the flock. Behind him are two women on horses; I guess (5)______ are his wife and daughter.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. like.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Here the blank needs a preposition of comparison. "Like" means "similar to / in the manner of" and is followed directly by a noun phrase — here, "a crowd of rowdy children".

◦ Correct: ... which carry him down the path like a crowd of rowdy children.

• The comparison is vivid: the milling sheep bustle around him just as a noisy crowd of children would.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "likeness" is a noun meaning resemblance — a noun cannot link the clause to the following noun phrase.

• Option 3 "likely" is an adjective/adverb meaning "probable/probably" and does not express comparison.

• Option 4 "liking" is a noun meaning fondness ("a liking for sweets").

NOTE

• "Like" (preposition) is followed by a noun/pronoun: "He runs like a deer."

• "As" (conjunction) is followed by a clause with a verb: "He runs as a deer runs."

• "As" is also used to mean "in the capacity of": "She works as a teacher."

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

A young man walks toward me with a stick slung across his back and a (1)______ of sheep at his feet, which carry him down the path (2)______ a crowd of rowdy children. An older man follows, weatherworn but still (3)______, a rifle over his left shoulder. He clicks his tongue to (4)______ the flock. Behind him are two women on horses; I guess (5)______ are his wife and daughter.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. strong.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The key word is the contrastive conjunction "but still". The older man is described as "weatherworn" (worn and aged by exposure to sun, wind and rain), and the contrast that follows must be a positive quality — he is aged in appearance but still strong. (फिर भी मज़बूत)

◦ Correct: An older man follows, weatherworn but still strong, a rifle over his left shoulder.

• The detail of a rifle carried over his shoulder while walking supports the sense of continuing physical strength.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "sick", 3 "thin" and 4 "slow" are all negative/weakening descriptions. Placing any of them after "but still" destroys the contrast, because "weatherworn" is already negative.

NOTE

• Contrast markers such as but, yet, still, although, though, however, nevertheless, in spite of always signal that the idea after them opposes the idea before them. Spotting them is the fastest way to solve cloze questions.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

A young man walks toward me with a stick slung across his back and a (1)______ of sheep at his feet, which carry him down the path (2)______ a crowd of rowdy children. An older man follows, weatherworn but still (3)______, a rifle over his left shoulder. He clicks his tongue to (4)______ the flock. Behind him are two women on horses; I guess (5)______ are his wife and daughter.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. encourage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A shepherd clicks his tongue as a signal to urge his animals along. "Encourage" means to urge on, to give support or confidence so that someone/something keeps going, which is exactly what the clicking sound does to the flock. (प्रोत्साहित करना / हाँकना)

◦ Correct: He clicks his tongue to encourage the flock.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "punish" (to penalise for wrongdoing) makes no sense — a click of the tongue punishes nothing.

• Option 2 "claim" (to demand as one's right) is unrelated to driving animals.

• Option 4 "dress" (to put clothes on) is absurd in the context of sheep.

NOTE

• Verb + object collocations for herding: drive the flock, urge on the herd, round up the cattle, herd the sheep, encourage the animals forward.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

A young man walks toward me with a stick slung across his back and a (1)______ of sheep at his feet, which carry him down the path (2)______ a crowd of rowdy children. An older man follows, weatherworn but still (3)______, a rifle over his left shoulder. He clicks his tongue to (4)______ the flock. Behind him are two women on horses; I guess (5)______ are his wife and daughter.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. they.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is the subject of the verb "are" in the noun clause "I guess (that) ______ are his wife and daughter". A subject pronoun referring to two women is required, so the third-person plural subject pronoun "they" is correct.

◦ Correct: Behind him are two women on horses; I guess they are his wife and daughter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "them" is an object pronoun and cannot be the subject of "are".

• Option 2 "these" is a demonstrative used for things/people near the speaker; the women are at a distance behind the man, and "they" is the natural anaphoric reference.

• Option 4 "this" is singular and cannot agree with the plural verb "are" or refer to two women.

NOTE

• Subject pronouns: I, we, you, he, she, it, they. Object pronouns: me, us, you, him, her, it, them.

• Demonstratives: this/these (near), that/those (far); this/that are singular, these/those are plural.

question: Which of the following vitamins helps to keep our skin and eyes healthy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vitamin A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vitamin A (Retinol) is essential for healthy skin and good eyesight. It forms rhodopsin, the light-sensitive pigment of the retina, and maintains the health of epithelial (skin and mucous-membrane) tissue. (विटामिन A — त्वचा और आँखों के लिए)

• Its deficiency causes night blindness (nyctalopia), xerophthalmia (dryness of the eye) and rough, dry skin.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sources of Vitamin A: carrots, green leafy vegetables, papaya, mango, milk, butter, egg yolk, cod-liver oil. Plant sources supply beta-carotene, which the body converts into Vitamin A.

• Vitamin D (Calciferol) — bones and teeth; deficiency causes rickets/osteomalacia.

• Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) — immunity and gums; deficiency causes scurvy.

• Vitamin B complex — deficiency of B1 causes beriberi, of B3 pellagra, of B12 pernicious anaemia.

NOTE

• Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K. Water-soluble vitamins: B-complex and C.

• Vitamin A is also called the "anti-infective vitamin" because it protects the linings of the respiratory and digestive tracts.

question: According to the 2011 census, what is the literacy rate of New Delhi District?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 88.01 percent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of 2011, the literacy rate of the New Delhi district was 88.01 percent. (नई दिल्ली ज़िले की साक्षरता दर — 88.01 प्रतिशत)

• Literacy in the Census is measured for the population aged 7 years and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census of India and the 7th after Independence. Its motto was "Our Census, Our Future".

• India's overall literacy rate in 2011 was 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%).

• Kerala had the highest literacy rate among states (94%) and Bihar the lowest (61.8%); Lakshadweep was the highest among UTs.

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years under the Census Act, 1948, by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The first complete census was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

question: India accounts for what percent of total geographical area of the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.4 percent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India occupies about 2.4 percent of the world's total geographical (land) area, while supporting roughly 17–18 percent of the world's population. (विश्व के भू-क्षेत्र का लगभग 2.4 प्रतिशत)

• India's total area is 3.287 million sq km, making it the 7th largest country in the world by area.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The seven largest countries by area: Russia, Canada, USA, China, Brazil, Australia, India.

• India's mainland extends from 8°4' N to 37°6' N latitude and 68°7' E to 97°25' E longitude.

• India's land frontier is about 15,200 km and its total coastline (including islands) is about 7,516.6 km.

NOTE

• The Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) divides India almost into two halves, passing through eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

question: Which Guru of Kuchipudi dance form received Padma Bhushan in the year 1998?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam (1929–2012), the legendary maestro of the Kuchipudi dance form of Andhra Pradesh, was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1998. (वेम्पति चिन्ना सत्यम — कुचिपुड़ी)

• He founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Chennai (1963) and choreographed many celebrated dance-dramas, taking Kuchipudi from village performance to the international stage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Uday Shankar was a pioneer of modern/creative dance in India.

• Kelucharan Mohapatra was the greatest exponent of Odissi (Odisha).

• Guru Bipin Singh was the doyen of Manipuri dance.

NOTE

• Kuchipudi originates from the village of Kuchelapuram in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh. It combines nritta, nritya and natya, and its famous items include the Tarangam (dancing on the rim of a brass plate) and Bhama Kalapam.

• The eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: The Jain temple at Pattadakal was built by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rashtrakutas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Jain temple (Jaina Narayana temple) at Pattadakal, in the Bagalkot district of Karnataka, was built by the Rashtrakutas in the 9th century CE, most likely during the reign of Amoghavarsha I or Krishna II. (पट्टडकल का जैन मंदिर — राष्ट्रकूट)

• The rest of the Pattadakal group of monuments was built mainly by the Chalukyas of Badami, which is why this Jain temple stands apart from the main cluster.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Pattadakal was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987. It is famous for the blend of Nagara (North Indian) and Dravida (South Indian) temple styles.

• The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built by Queen Lokamahadevi to commemorate her husband Vikramaditya II's victory over the Pallavas of Kanchipuram.

• Nearby heritage sites: Badami (cave temples) and Aihole (called the "cradle of Indian temple architecture").

NOTE

• The Rashtrakutas (8th–10th century CE) ruled from Manyakheta and are best known for the magnificent rock-cut Kailasa temple at Ellora, built by Krishna I.

question: Which among the following states has the highest sex ratio in India according to the Census 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census 2011, Kerala had the highest sex ratio among Indian states — 1084 females per 1000 males. (केरल — सर्वाधिक लिंगानुपात)

• Sex ratio is defined in India as the number of females per 1000 males.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India's overall sex ratio in 2011 was 943 females per 1000 males (up from 933 in 2001).

• Haryana had the lowest sex ratio among states (879); among Union Territories, Puducherry was highest (1037) and Daman & Diu lowest (618).

• The child sex ratio (0–6 years) in 2011 was 919, the lowest since Independence — a matter of serious concern.

NOTE

• Kerala also leads India in literacy (94%), life expectancy and the Human Development Index, largely due to its investments in education and public health.

• The scheme "Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao" (launched 2015 from Panipat, Haryana) targets the declining child sex ratio.

question: Which among the following elements is used in moisturising creams and soaps because of its hygroscopic properties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Glycerol.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Glycerol (glycerine, propane-1,2,3-triol) is strongly hygroscopic — it absorbs and retains moisture from the air. This is why it is added to moisturising creams, lotions, soaps and cosmetics to keep the skin soft and hydrated. (ग्लिसरॉल — नमी सोखने वाला)

• It is a colourless, odourless, sweet-tasting, viscous liquid and is a by-product of soap manufacture (saponification) of fats and oils.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Galena is the chief ore of lead (PbS) — lead sulphide.

• Ethanol (C2H5OH) is an alcohol used in beverages, sanitisers and as a fuel additive; it is drying rather than moisturising.

• Freon is the trade name for chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) once used as refrigerants; they damage the ozone layer and were phased out under the Montreal Protocol (1987).

NOTE

• Glycerol is also used to make nitroglycerine (an explosive and a heart medicine), in food as a sweetener/humectant, and in pharmaceutical syrups.

• A hygroscopic substance absorbs moisture from air; other examples are silica gel, calcium chloride and concentrated sulphuric acid.

question: Which UK Prime Minister resigned on 20th October, 2022 after serving for 44 days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Liz Truss.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Liz Truss announced her resignation as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom on 20 October 2022, after just 44 days in office — the shortest tenure of any British Prime Minister in history. (लिज़ ट्रस — मात्र 44 दिन)

• Her resignation followed the market turmoil triggered by her government's "mini-budget" of large unfunded tax cuts, which caused the pound to fall sharply.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• She had taken office on 6 September 2022, succeeding Boris Johnson, who resigned amid a series of political scandals.

• She was succeeded by Rishi Sunak, who became the first British Prime Minister of Indian origin on 25 October 2022.

• Theresa May was UK Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019 (the second woman to hold the post after Margaret Thatcher).

NOTE

• The UK is a constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary democracy. Queen Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022 — just two days after appointing Liz Truss — and was succeeded by King Charles III.

question: Who among the following has been awarded with Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2021 for “Para Shooting”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Avani Lekhara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Avani Lekhara received the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2021 for Para Shooting. (अवनि लेखरा — पैरा निशानेबाज़ी)

• At the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics (held in 2021) she won a gold medal in the 10 m Air Rifle Standing SH1 event and a bronze in the 50 m Rifle 3 Positions SH1, becoming the first Indian woman to win a Paralympic gold.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Krishna Nagar won gold in para badminton (SH6) and Pramod Bhagat gold in para badminton (SL3) at Tokyo.

• Sumit Antil won gold in the men's javelin throw F64 with a world record.

• All of them were also honoured in the same year's national sports awards.

NOTE

• The Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award was renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in August 2021. It is India's highest sporting honour.

• Major Dhyan Chand — "The Wizard" of hockey — won Olympic golds in 1928, 1932 and 1936; his birthday, 29 August, is celebrated as National Sports Day.

question: The prehistoric period in the early development of human beings is commonly known as the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Old stone age.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Old Stone Age (Palaeolithic Age) is the earliest prehistoric period in the development of human beings. It covers roughly 2 million BCE to 10,000 BCE. (पुरापाषाण काल)

• In this age humans were hunter-gatherers, used rough, unpolished stone tools (hand-axes, cleavers, choppers), lived in caves and rock shelters, and did not know agriculture, pottery or metals. The discovery of fire belongs to this age.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mesolithic (Middle Stone Age, c. 10,000–6000 BCE) — use of tiny tools called microliths; beginning of animal domestication; famous site Bhimbetka (Madhya Pradesh) with rock paintings.

• Neolithic / New Stone Age (c. 6000–1000 BCE) — polished stone tools, beginning of agriculture, pottery and settled village life; sites like Mehrgarh, Burzahom and Chirand.

• Iron Age comes much later, after the Chalcolithic (copper-stone) and Bronze ages.

NOTE

• The Indian Palaeolithic is divided into Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic. Important sites: Soan valley, Bhimbetka, Hunsgi, Attirampakkam and Belan valley.

question: Which among the following is NOT a Jovian planet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mercury.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Jovian planets (also called gas giants or outer planets) are Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. They are large, gaseous, low in density and have many moons and ring systems.

• Mercury is not a Jovian planet — it is a terrestrial (rocky/inner) planet, along with Venus, Earth and Mars. (बुध — स्थलीय ग्रह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun; it has the shortest year (88 Earth days) and no natural satellite.

• Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System; Saturn is famous for its bright rings and is the least dense planet (it would float on water).

• Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun and is called the windiest planet.

NOTE

• "Jovian" comes from Jove, another name for the Roman god Jupiter.

• Terrestrial planets are separated from the Jovian planets by the asteroid belt lying between Mars and Jupiter.

question: Article 17 of the Indian constitution is related with ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abolition of Untouchability.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 17 of the Indian Constitution abolishes "untouchability" and forbids its practice in any form. The enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability is a punishable offence. (अनुच्छेद 17 — अस्पृश्यता का अंत)

• It is one of the few Fundamental Rights available against private individuals as well as the State, and it is absolute — no exceptions are permitted.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 14 — Equality before law and equal protection of the laws.

• Article 15 — Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

• Article 16 — Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.

• Article 18 — Abolition of titles.

• Article 21A — Right to Education (added by the 86th Amendment, 2002, for children aged 6–14).

NOTE

• Articles 14–18 together constitute the Right to Equality.

• Parliament enacted the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, renamed the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, and later the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 to enforce Article 17.

question: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, famous Indian scientist's, autobiography is known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wings of Fire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wings of Fire: An Autobiography" is the autobiography of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, co-written with Arun Tiwari and published in 1999. (विंग्स ऑफ फायर — डॉ. ए.पी.जे. अब्दुल कलाम की आत्मकथा)

• It traces his journey from a humble childhood in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu, to becoming the architect of India's missile programme.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dr. Kalam was the 11th President of India (2002–2007), popularly called the "Missile Man of India" and the "People's President". He received the Bharat Ratna in 1997.

• His other books: India 2020, Ignited Minds, My Journey, Turning Points, Transcendence.

• One Life is Not Enough — autobiography of K. Natwar Singh; Waiting for a Visa — autobiographical notes of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar; The Race of My Life — autobiography of Milkha Singh.

NOTE

• Dr. Kalam worked at ISRO and DRDO; he was the project director of India's first indigenous satellite launch vehicle SLV-III, which put Rohini into orbit in 1980, and played a key role in the Pokhran-II nuclear tests of 1998.

• His birthday, 15 October, is observed as World Students' Day.

question: Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma, an Indian musician and composer was the foremost exponent of the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Santoor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma (1938–2022) was the foremost exponent of the Santoor, a hundred-stringed trapezoid instrument of Jammu and Kashmir. (पंडित शिवकुमार शर्मा — संतूर)

• He is credited with transforming the santoor from a folk instrument of Kashmiri Sufiana music into a full-fledged Indian classical concert instrument.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He was awarded the Padma Shri (1991) and the Padma Vibhushan (2001).

• Along with flautist Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, he composed music for films such as Silsila, Chandni, Lamhe and Darr under the joint name "Shiv–Hari".

• The santoor is played with a pair of light wooden mallets called "kalam".

NOTE

• Classification of Indian instruments: Tata Vadya (stringed — sitar, sarod, veena), Sushira Vadya (wind — flute, shehnai), Avanaddha Vadya (percussion with membrane — tabla, mridangam) and Ghana Vadya (solid/struck — manjira, jaltarang). The santoor is a struck stringed instrument.

question: Which among the following sessions of Indian National Congress was the first session to be presided by a lady?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcutta - 1917.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1917 was presided over by Dr. Annie Besant, who thus became the first woman President of the INC. (कलकत्ता अधिवेशन 1917 — एनी बेसेंट)

• She was an Irish-born theosophist and social reformer who founded the Home Rule League (1916) and the newspaper New India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kanpur session, 1925 — presided over by Sarojini Naidu, the first Indian woman President of the INC (the "Nightingale of India").

• Lahore session, 1929 — presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru; it adopted the resolution of "Purna Swaraj" (complete independence), and 26 January 1930 was observed as the first Independence Day.

• Surat session, 1907 — the famous Surat Split between the Moderates and the Extremists; presided over by Rash Behari Ghosh.

NOTE

• The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A. O. Hume; its first session (Bombay, 1885) was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.

• Nellie Sengupta presided over the Calcutta session of 1933 — the third woman to head the Congress.

question: The Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 aimed at unifying the ______ Municipal Corporations of Delhi to ensure a robust setup for synergised and strategic planning and optimal utilisation of resources.
solution_text:
The correct answer is three.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Act, 2022 merged the three municipal corporations of Delhi — the North Delhi Municipal Corporation, South Delhi Municipal Corporation and East Delhi Municipal Corporation — back into a single unified Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD). (तीन निगमों का एकीकरण)

• The stated aim was synergised and strategic planning, optimal utilisation of resources and a financially stronger civic body.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Municipal Corporation of Delhi was originally created under the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, and was trifurcated in 2012.

• The Bill was passed by Parliament in April 2022 and came into force from 22 May 2022. It also reduced the number of wards to not more than 250.

NOTE

• Urban local bodies were given constitutional status by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which added Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects) to the Constitution.

• Types of urban local bodies: Municipal Corporation (large cities), Municipality/Municipal Council (smaller cities) and Nagar Panchayat (transitional areas).

question: The Walker Cup is associated with which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Golf.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Walker Cup is a golf trophy. It is contested every two years between teams of amateur golfers from the United States and a combined team from Great Britain and Ireland. (वॉकर कप — गोल्फ)

• It is named after George Herbert Walker, a former president of the United States Golf Association, and was first played in 1922.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other golf trophies: Ryder Cup (USA vs Europe, professionals), Solheim Cup (women professionals), Presidents Cup, and the four majors — The Masters, US Open, The Open Championship and PGA Championship.

• Hockey trophies: Agha Khan Cup, Beighton Cup, Dhyan Chand Trophy, Rangaswami Cup.

• Chess: Linares Trophy, Khel Ratna is national; Football: FIFA World Cup, Durand Cup, Santosh Trophy.

NOTE

• Golf terms: birdie (one under par), eagle (two under par), bogey (one over par), par, albatross, hole-in-one, caddie, tee, putt.

• India's leading golfers include Jeev Milkha Singh, Anirban Lahiri and Aditi Ashok.

question: Galvanisation is a process in which a protective ______ coating is applied on iron to prevent it from rusting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is zinc.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Galvanisation is the process of applying a protective coating of zinc on iron or steel to prevent rusting (corrosion). (जस्ता / ज़िंक की परत चढ़ाना)

• Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes in preference to the iron beneath — this is called sacrificial protection. Even if the coating is scratched, the exposed iron remains protected.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Rust is hydrated ferric oxide (Fe2O3·xH2O); rusting requires both oxygen (air) and moisture (water).

• Other methods of preventing corrosion: painting, greasing/oiling, electroplating, anodising, alloying (e.g., stainless steel).

• Electroplating with chromium, nickel or silver is done mainly for shine and wear resistance, not sacrificial protection.

NOTE

• Zinc (Zn) — atomic number 30. Galvanised iron sheets (GI sheets) are widely used for roofing, buckets, pipes and fencing.

• Stainless steel is an alloy of iron, chromium (about 18%) and nickel (about 8%) and does not rust.

question: Which among the following is the famous harvest festival of Meghalaya, India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nongkrem festival.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Ka Pomblang Nongkrem" (Nongkrem Dance festival) is the famous harvest/thanksgiving festival of the Khasi tribe of Meghalaya. It is held annually at Smit, near Shillong. (नोंगक्रेम — मेघालय)

• It is a five-day religious festival in which the Khasis thank the deity Ka Blei Synshar for a good harvest and pray for peace and prosperity; a goat sacrifice (Pomblang) is a central ritual.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Chapchar Kut is the spring festival of Mizoram, celebrated after the completion of jhum (slash-and-burn) clearing.

• Hornbill festival is the "Festival of Festivals" of Nagaland, held at Kisama every December.

• Sunburn is a commercial electronic dance music festival held in Goa/Pune, not a tribal harvest festival.

NOTE

• Other festivals of Meghalaya: Wangala (the hundred-drums harvest festival of the Garo tribe), Behdienkhlam (of the Jaintia tribe) and Shad Suk Mynsiem (the spring dance of the Khasis).

• Meghalaya, "the abode of clouds", was carved out of Assam in 1972; its capital is Shillong.

question: Bharatanatyam dance is associated with which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, one of the oldest classical dances of India. (भरतनाट्यम — तमिलनाडु)

• It grew out of the Sadir/Dasiattam performed by devadasis in the temples of Tamil Nadu and is based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Its repertoire follows a fixed order: Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, Tillana and Shlokam.

• Famous exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale (who founded Kalakshetra), Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam and Vyjayanthimala.

• The name is often explained as BHAva (expression) + RAga (melody) + TAla (rhythm) + Natyam (dance).

NOTE

• Classical dances and their states: Bharatanatyam – Tamil Nadu; Kathak – Uttar Pradesh; Kathakali & Mohiniyattam – Kerala; Kuchipudi – Andhra Pradesh; Odissi – Odisha; Manipuri – Manipur; Sattriya – Assam.

• Folk dances: Lavani – Maharashtra; Garba – Gujarat; Bhangra – Punjab; Bihu – Assam.

question: Indian Railways plan to become Net Zero Carbon Emitter by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2030.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Indian Railways has set the target of becoming a "Net Zero Carbon Emitter" by 2030, which would make it the world's first railway system to achieve net-zero carbon emissions. (2030 तक नेट ज़ीरो कार्बन उत्सर्जक)

• The plan rests on 100% electrification of broad-gauge routes, large-scale use of solar and wind energy, energy-efficient locomotives, head-on generation in coaches and extensive afforestation along tracks.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Indian Railways is the fourth largest railway network in the world (after the USA, China and Russia) and one of the world's largest employers.

• The first passenger train in India ran from Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane on 16 April 1853, a distance of about 34 km.

• India as a nation has announced a net-zero target of 2070 (declared by the Prime Minister at COP26, Glasgow, 2021, as part of the "Panchamrit" commitments).

NOTE

• "Net zero" means balancing the greenhouse gases emitted with an equivalent amount removed or offset, so that the net addition to the atmosphere is zero.

question: What does ‘F’ stand for in FRBM Act, 2003 of Indian economy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fiscal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• FRBM stands for the "Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management" Act, so the letter "F" stands for "Fiscal". (राजकोषीय उत्तरदायित्व एवं बजट प्रबंधन अधिनियम)

• The Act was passed in 2003 and came into force in July 2004. Its objective is to bring fiscal discipline, reduce the fiscal deficit and public debt, and ensure inter-generational equity in fiscal management.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The FRBM Act required the government to reduce the fiscal deficit to 3% of GDP and eliminate the revenue deficit.

• It mandates the presentation of statements along with the Budget: the Medium Term Fiscal Policy Statement, the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement and the Macro-Economic Framework Statement.

• The N. K. Singh Committee (2017) reviewed the Act and recommended a debt-to-GDP ratio of 60% (40% Centre + 20% States) as the medium-term anchor.

NOTE

• Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure – Total receipts (excluding borrowings).

• Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure – Revenue receipts.

• Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit – Interest payments.

question: Who among the following introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital - the two basic coins of the Sultanate period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iltutmish.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shamsuddin Iltutmish (r. 1211–1236) introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital, which became the two basic coins of the Delhi Sultanate. (इल्तुतमिश — चाँदी का टंका और ताँबे का जीतल)

• The silver tanka weighed about 175 grains and was the ancestor of the modern rupee; the jital was the small change used in everyday transactions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Iltutmish belonged to the Slave (Mamluk/Ilbari) dynasty and is regarded as the real consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate. He shifted the capital from Lahore to Delhi, created the Iqta system and the nobility group known as the "Chahalgani/Turkan-i-Chihalgani" (Corps of Forty).

• He completed the Qutub Minar begun by Qutubuddin Aibak, and obtained a letter of investiture (mansur) from the Abbasid Caliph in 1229, giving legal status to his rule.

• Alauddin Khilji is famous for market/price control regulations; Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced token currency; Ibrahim Lodi was defeated at Panipat (1526) by Babur.

NOTE

• Dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate in order: Slave (1206–90), Khilji (1290–1320), Tughlaq (1320–1414), Sayyid (1414–51) and Lodi (1451–1526).

question: Which of the following states is the leading producer of cotton in India, as of November 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gujarat is the leading producer of cotton in India (as of November 2022), followed by Maharashtra and Telangana. (गुजरात — कपास का सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक)

• The black soil (regur/black cotton soil) of the Deccan Trap region, which retains moisture well, together with a warm climate and moderate rainfall, makes Gujarat ideal for cotton cultivation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Cotton is a kharif crop, sown around June–July and harvested from October onwards; it needs 21–30°C temperature, 50–100 cm rainfall and about 210 frost-free days.

• India is among the largest producers of cotton in the world along with China and the USA.

• Cotton is called "white gold" and is the mainstay of India's textile industry.

NOTE

• Leading producers of other crops: Rice – West Bengal; Wheat – Uttar Pradesh; Sugarcane – Uttar Pradesh; Jute – West Bengal; Tea – Assam; Coffee – Karnataka; Groundnut – Gujarat; Pulses – Madhya Pradesh.

question: Who was the President of Swaraj Party formed in the year 1922?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chittaranjan Das.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Swaraj Party was formed on 1 January 1923 (following the Gaya session of the Congress in December 1922) with Chittaranjan Das (Deshbandhu) as its President and Motilal Nehru as its Secretary. (चित्तरंजन दास — अध्यक्ष, स्वराज पार्टी)

• It arose after the sudden withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement (February 1922) following the Chauri Chaura incident.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Swarajists (called "Pro-changers") wanted to enter the legislative councils and obstruct the government from within; the "No-changers" (Rajendra Prasad, Sardar Patel, C. Rajagopalachari) opposed council entry and favoured constructive village work.

• The party did well in the 1923 elections to the Central Legislative Assembly and provincial councils, and blocked several government proposals.

• C. R. Das was known as "Deshbandhu"; he defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case and the Chittagong/Barisal accused, and died in 1925.

NOTE

• The Swaraj Party functioned as a group within the Congress, not as a separate rival organisation. After C. R. Das's death in 1925 the party gradually weakened.
